title: A regular singularity as two linear maps
notes: On a disk, the category is described by \(\Psi\mathrel{\mathop{\rightleftarrows}^{u}_{v}}\Phi\) with \(uv-\mathrm{Id}\) invertible; outside zero there is a bundle with connection.

fate: The disk equivalence is \citet[Corollary 3.2]{beilinson1987glue}, written from 1982 notes and published in 1987.

title: Liouville action from the string conformal factor
notes: In isothermal coordinates \(g_{ab}=e^\varphi\delta_{ab}\), \(S=\gamma^{-1}\int(\tfrac12|\nabla\varphi|^2+e^\varphi)\), with \(\gamma^{-1}=(26-D)/(48\pi)\).

title: Bosonic oscillators realize the Virasoro algebra
notes: For positive n the notes write \(L_n=(\alpha+i\beta n)a_n+\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}a_ka_{n-k}+\sum_{k\ge1}a_k^+a_{n+k}\), with \([a_n,a_m^+]=n\delta_{nm}\).

title: Oscillator and Verma bases agree only generically
notes: The vectors \(a_{n_1}^+a_{n_2}^+\cdots|0\rangle\) and \(L_{-n_1}L_{-n_2}\cdots|0\rangle\) are said to be mutually expressible; the former are orthogonal.
statement: Normalized occupation-number vectors form an orthogonal Fock basis. The change from Virasoro descendants is invertible at a fixed level only when the corresponding transition matrix has nonzero determinant. Singular vectors and special parameters can make the Verma-to-Fock map fail to be an isomorphism.

title: Quadratic current and the Miura-type stress tensor
notes: \(T=p^{\prime}+p^2\), with a formal mode expansion of p.
statement: The classical relation expresses a projective connection as a quadratic current plus a derivative. In the quantum oscillator realization the quadratic product must be normally ordered, and its derivative coefficient, zero mode and Laurent powers must match the chosen central charge. title: Bargmann coordinates turn Ward identities into PDEs
notes: Put \(a_n=\partial_{z_n}\), \(a_n^+=nz_n\), then write a differential equation for \(F(x,z_1,z_2,\ldots)\).
statement: On polynomials in oscillator coordinates these operators satisfy the stated Heisenberg relations. Substitution into the corrected \(L_n\) gives \([(\alpha+i\beta n)\partial_{z_n}+\tfrac12\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\partial_{z_k}\partial_{z_{n-k}}+\sum_{k\ge1}kz_k\partial_{z_{n+k}}]F=(x^{n+1}\partial_x+(n+1)hx^n)F\), provided F is the corresponding highest-weight matrix element.

title: Reconstructing four-point correlations from conformal blocks
notes: The notes propose computing the coefficients algebraically and thereby determining \(\Psi\).
statement: Ward identities determine descendants within a specified channel. A full four-point function additionally needs primary spectrum, three-point constants, a pairing of chiral and antichiral blocks, and an integration or summation prescription. The notebook does not supply those data.

title: The planar domain wall and its thickness

Its characteristic width is of order \((\lambda\eta)^{-1}\); its energy is finite per unit area, not finite over the whole infinite plane.

title: Local U(1) covariance of the Abelian Higgs action
notes: The covariant derivative is \(\partial+iA\), but the printed transformation has \(\varphi\mapsto e^{i\alpha}\varphi\), \(A\mapsto A+d\alpha\).

title: Vortex winding and flux quantization
notes: A transverse circuit rotates the vacuum vector once; \(\varphi_1=(x/r)f(r)\), \(\varphi_2=(y/r)f(r)\), approaching the vacuum at infinity.

title: The thin-core approximation produces a string action

title: Worldsheet area and extremality
notes: The moving string sweeps a sheet; its area is called the Lagrangian, followed by minimum area.
statement: The induced worldsheet metric is \(h_{ab}=\eta_{\mu\nu}\partial_aX^\mu\partial_bX^\nu\). The Nambu--Goto action is proportional to its Lorentzian area. Its Euler--Lagrange equations express stationarity, equivalently vanishing mean-curvature vector for a smooth timelike immersion, with suitable boundary conditions. title: A circular loop contracts in the effective model
notes: A ring-shaped string contracts, quickly reaches the speed of light and becomes a small lump.

title: Weighted pullback extends the Möbius action
notes: A fractional-linear action with a factor \(|\beta z+\delta|^\lambda\) is extended to diffeomorphisms by \(f\mapsto(f\circ\varphi^{-1})|D\varphi^{-1}|^{-\lambda/2}\).
statement: For any real density weight a, \(T_a(\varphi)f=(f\circ\varphi^{-1})|(\varphi^{-1})^{\prime}|^a\) defines a representation of orientation-preserving smooth circle diffeomorphisms on smooth densities in a local trivialization. Its restriction to Möbius transformations has the familiar multiplier. Unitarity depends on the Hilbert form and parameter; it does not follow from the extension formula.

title: The complementary-series inner product is almost invariant
notes: The imaginary part of a double integral with kernel \(|x_1-x_2|^{-2+\lambda}/\Gamma(-1+\lambda)\) is Möbius invariant; under general diffeomorphisms the operator is marked \(U(1+\mathrm{HS})\).
statement: For Neretin’s positive complementary-series Hilbert completions, with his parameter \(0<\rho<2\), \(\rho\ne1\), the weighted pullbacks are bounded invertible and have polar form \(O(1+K)\), with K Hilbert--Schmidt. In that range they are orthogonal exactly for Möbius transformations. Analytic continuation and a parameter-dependent normalization are required outside the convergent integral range.
reconstruction: The positivity range is stated in the publication’s parameter, not asserted for every value of the handwritten lambda. The imaginary-part form is on the complexification of the positive real Hilbert space.

title: Gaussian unitarization on Fock space
notes: The margin corrects the phrase unitarily: the weighted action is nonunitary, but unitary representations are constructed on Fock space using coherent states.
statement: If a real Hilbert-space representation takes values in \(GL_0(H)=\{O(1+K):K\text{ Hilbert--Schmidt}\}\), the associated transformations of a Gaussian realization are quasi-invariant. Composition multiplied by the square root of the Radon--Nikodym derivative gives a unitary representation on Gaussian \(L^2\), equivalently the symmetric Fock space. This changes the representation space.
fate: \citet[section 1 and the construction after Theorem 1]{neretin1982complementary} gives exactly this mechanism. Its restriction to the Möbius subgroup is a Fock representation, not the original single complementary-series representation.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: The loop-space symplectic form modulo constants
notes: For maps \(f,g:S^1\to\mathbb R^d\), with a Riemannian or Lorentzian target metric, use \(\omega(f,g)=\int_{S^1}(f,dg)\); quotient by constant maps.
statement: For a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form b on \(\mathbb R^d\), the form \(\omega(f,g)=\int b(f,g^{\prime})dt\) on smooth loops is skew by integration by parts. Its radical is exactly the constant loops, so it descends to a weak symplectic form on \(C^\infty(S^1,\mathbb R^d)/\mathbb R^d\). Orientation-preserving reparametrizations preserve it. Positivity of b is unnecessary for this algebraic assertion.
reconstruction: Smoothness, orientation, nondegeneracy of the target metric and weak rather than strong symplectic topology are made explicit.
fate: This is the classical oscillator phase space underlying the final construction in \citet{feigin1984semiinfinite}; the scalar endpoint realization is already in \citet[section 4]{neretin1982complementary}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: The quotient carries a Poisson algebra, not automatically a smooth manifold
notes: The space \(V^{\prime}/\operatorname{Diff}S^1\) is said to have a Hamiltonian structure.
statement: Invariant observables in a symplectic Poisson algebra are closed under the bracket when the action preserves the symplectic structure. This defines a quotient Poisson algebra. A smooth Poisson manifold structure on the orbit space additionally requires a suitable regular quotient; the loop-space quotient in the notebook is generally singular and no such manifold theorem is established.
reconstruction: The algebra of observables is the precise interpretation supported without additional regularity hypotheses.
fate: The finite-dimensional reduction principle is older \citep{marsdenweinstein1974reduction}. Its infinite-dimensional application here is formal unless a class of admissible observables and a quotient category are chosen.

title: Symplectic reduction requires a moment-map level
notes: Kirillov describes a reduced symplectic manifold and says the invariant Poisson bracket is degenerate and one must take a quotient.
statement: For a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian G-action with equivariant moment map \(\mu\), if \(\xi\) is a regular value and \(G_\xi\) acts freely and properly on \(\mu^{-1}(\xi)\), then \(\mu^{-1}(\xi)/G_\xi\) is symplectic, with reduced form characterized by pullback. The full orbit space \(M/G\) is not generally symplectic.
reconstruction: The level set, Hamiltonian hypothesis and free proper regularity assumptions are restored editorially.
fate: This is the regular reduction construction of \citet{marsdenweinstein1974reduction}, published in 1974.

title: Polarization and the symmetric oscillator space
notes: Complexify \(V^{\prime}=H^+\oplus H^-\), using Fourier modes analytic inside and outside the circle; the notes display \(\Phi=\bigoplus_i S^iH_+\).
statement: A positive/negative Fourier polarization gives two paired complex Lagrangian spaces. The algebraic bosonic Fock module is a symmetric algebra on the creation space; annihilation acts by contractions with the dual polarization. Which summand is labelled plus is conventional. A Hilbert completion and positive inner product need an additional choice; a Lorentzian target does not provide a positive Hilbert norm by itself.

title: The Schwinger term obstructs ordinary invariants
notes: The map from vector fields through symplectic transformations to the Weyl representation is projective; a Schwinger term appears and invariants do not exist.
statement: The quantized action factors through the Virasoro central extension. In a module on which its central element acts by a nonzero scalar, no nonzero vector is annihilated by every Virasoro generator including the center. For d free scalar oscillators with standard normal ordering, the matter central charge is d, also for a nondegenerate indefinite target form.

fate: The central extension is older \citep{gelfandfuchs1968circle}; Feigin’s string construction explicitly treats the resulting central charge \citep[Example 1 and final paragraph]{feigin1984semiinfinite}.

title: Physical states as an image of invariants in coinvariants
notes: For \(L_+=\langle L_1,L_2,\ldots\rangle\), \(L_-=\langle L_{-1},L_{-2},\ldots\rangle\), take the image of \(\Phi^{L_+}\to\Phi/L_-\Phi\), then select an \(L_0\) condition.

Physical states require a further zero-mode condition, \(e_0v=-v\) in Feigin’s sign convention. Thus invariants are retained only modulo spurious negative-mode states; they are not the full Virasoro-invariant subspace.

title: The critical charge 26 in semi-infinite homology
notes: The resulting space is nontrivial at least for \(d=26\).

title: The periodic Hilbert transform is a complex structure modulo constants

With the displayed sign convention, H acts on nonzero Fourier modes by \(i\operatorname{sgn}(n)\), and \(H^2=-1\) on mean-zero functions or the quotient by constants. title: Two endpoint Hilbert forms

title: Endpoint actions preserve a symplectic form

On the function realization the form is, up to sign and normalization, \(\int f\,dg\). This stronger exact invariance is an endpoint statement, not a consequence of near-orthogonality at every parameter.

title: Normalized Hardy projections and Lagrangian subspaces

The unscaled \(H\pm i\) have those images but are not idempotents.

title: The logarithmic Hilbert convolution is not a delta derivative
notes: The integral \(\int\log|(t-s)/2|\,(s-\sigma)^{-1}ds\) is expected to give \(\delta^{\prime}\), with analytic continuation proposed.

title: Hamiltonian torus actions and the moment map
notes: A torus acts symplectically, each infinitesimal field has a Hamiltonian, and the Hamiltonians commute; equivalently, give commuting functions with periodic flows. The map is \(\mu(m)(X)=H_X(m)\).
statement: Let a torus T act on a compact connected symplectic manifold \((M,\omega)\). A Hamiltonian action has a T-invariant map \(\mu:M\to\mathfrak t^*\) satisfying \(d\langle\mu,X\rangle=\iota_{X_M}\omega\), with the sign convention fixed accordingly. Conversely, commuting complete Hamiltonian flows whose joint period lattice defines T give such an action. Individual periodicity alone does not specify an effective torus of the claimed rank.
reconstruction: Connectedness, the period lattice and moment-map sign are supplied; the later paper is exposition of the named 1982 theorem.
fate: The setting is explicit in \citet[section 6]{atiyahbott1984moment}, explaining the already published 1982 result \citep{duistermaatheckman1982variation}.

title: The cocycle behind commuting Hamiltonian fields
notes: Commuting fields need not come from Poisson-commuting Hamiltonians; the example uses y and minus x on the plane. The cocycle must be trivial.
statement: If Hamiltonian vector fields commute on connected M, their Poisson brackets are constant. These constants form a Lie-algebra 2-cocycle; an equivariant moment map requires its vanishing after the allowed normalization. For an abelian Lie algebra a nonzero such cocycle cannot be removed merely by adding constants. The plane translations illustrate this obstruction, but are not a periodic torus action on compact M.
reconstruction: The scope of the noncompact translation example and the distinction between a zero cocycle and an arbitrary cohomologically trivial representative are made explicit.
fate: This is the standard moment-map equivariance obstruction underlying \citet[section 6]{atiyahbott1984moment}. In the compact torus setting, averaging Hamiltonians gives an invariant moment map when the individual infinitesimal contractions are exact.

title: Orbit tangent spaces are isotropic

statement: For a Hamiltonian torus action, \(\omega(X_M,Y_M)=0\); hence each tangent space to a torus orbit is isotropic and can be extended to a Lagrangian linear subspace of \(T_mM\). This pointwise extension does not imply a globally defined Lagrangian foliation or polarization.

title: Regular symplectic reduction by the torus

statement: If \(\xi\) is a regular value and T acts freely on its level, \(M_\xi^{red}=\mu^{-1}(\xi)/T\) is a smooth symplectic manifold with reduced form \(\omega_\xi\). A locally free action gives the corresponding symplectic orbifold. The characteristic kernel on the level is the orbit tangent distribution. Singular values require a stratified reduction, absent from this elementary statement.

title: The reduced symplectic class varies affinely

statement: On a connected chamber of regular values, identify nearby reduced spaces by the regular family. Their de Rham classes vary affinely: \([\omega_\xi]=[\omega_{\xi_0}]+\langle\xi-\xi_0,c\rangle\), where c is the fixed curvature/Chern-class vector with a convention-dependent sign. This is a statement about cohomology under the family identifications, not pointwise linearity of differential forms on unrelated fibers.

title: Piecewise polynomial reduced volume and density
notes: The corollary is written \(\operatorname{vol}(M_\xi)\) is piecewise polynomial, although \(M_\xi\) was defined as the unreduced level set.
statement: For a \(2n\)-dimensional compact Hamiltonian manifold with effective torus dimension k, the reduced symplectic volume on a regular chamber is a polynomial of degree at most \(n-k\). With compatible Haar and Lebesgue normalizations, it is the density of the pushforward of Liouville measure by the moment map. The symplectic volume here belongs to the reduced \(2(n-k)\)-dimensional space, not the presymplectic level set.

title: Exact stationary phase for isolated fixed points
notes: The integral \(\int_Me^{iH_X}\,dm\) is exactly calculable by stationary phase.
statement: For a compact symplectic manifold with Hamiltonian torus action, choose X so that its zero set consists of isolated nondegenerate fixed points. With Liouville amplitude, the stationary-phase sum is exact: it is a finite sum of \(e^{itH_X(p)}\) divided by the product of the linearized weights evaluated at \(tX\), including the phase and measure-normalization factors. This assertion is special to the Hamiltonian setting and its canonical amplitude.

title: Positive-dimensional fixed components need the equivariant Euler class

The Euler denominator includes curvature/Chern classes of the normal bundle as well as its weights. Consequently it cannot in general be replaced by \(\operatorname{vol}(F)/\prod\lambda_j(X)\); that simplification is valid for isolated points and in special cases when higher characteristic contributions vanish.

title: Quadratic local phase and finite Fourier expansion force exactness

title: Catalan many minimal pencils on a general even-genus curve
notes: Griffiths and Harris count ways of obtaining one and the same surface as a covering; the answer is the Catalan sequence.
statement: A general smooth complex curve of genus \(2k\), \(k\ge1\), has \(C_k\) pencils of degree \(k+1\), equivalently maps to the projective line modulo target automorphisms, with \(6k\) simple branch points in the generic case. Special curves need not have this finite count.
reconstruction: Even genus, general curve, degree and equivalence under target automorphisms are recovered from the footnote rather than the abbreviated notebook.
fate: \citet[section 4, footnote]{arnold1983mathieu} states exactly this example and identifies Griffiths--Harris, Principles of Algebraic Geometry (1978), as the antecedent. The book’s result was not independently opened, so this historical attribution is indirect through Arnold’s primary paper.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: Bracket symbols as Catalan objects
notes: A properly formed string of letters and parentheses has length equal to letters plus opening parentheses; the number of shapes is Catalan.
statement: Consider balanced parenthesis words with nonempty contents in each pair, and letters serving as indistinguishable ordered slots. Give each letter and each opening parenthesis weight one. The shapes of length n are counted by \(C_n\); length two gives \(ab,(a)\), and length three gives five shapes. Letters become independently chosen quiver vertices only in a later filling.
reconstruction: Distinguishing abstract shapes from fillings prevents counting infinitely many alphabet choices.
fate: This exact notation and its counting appear in \citet[section 4]{arnold1983mathieu}, received 1 February and published later in 1983. The Supplement identifies the equivalent Catalan staircase diagrams in Bloch’s 1958 approach; A marks this particular presentation, not priority for Catalan perturbation theory.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: The spectral quiver and its chronological products
notes: The eigenspaces \(V_i\) are vertices and \(A_{ij}:V_i\to V_j\) are arrows. Products are taken following the arrows.
statement: Let \(\Lambda\) act as the distinct scalar \(\lambda_i\) on each block \(V_i\). Draw an arrow \(i\to j\) when the perturbing block \(A_{ij}\) is nonzero. For a path \(i_0\to i_1\to\cdots\to i_k\), its chronological product is \(A_{i_{k-1}i_k}\cdots A_{i_0i_1}:V_{i_0}\to V_{i_k}\), with composition read right to left.
reconstruction: The direction convention is fixed from the handwritten map, so no transposition of the block indices is silently introduced.
fate: \citet[section 1, definitions]{arnold1983mathieu} gives this exact quiver presentation. Diagrammatic perturbation itself is older, as the paper’s Supplement explicitly acknowledges.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: Local finiteness controls formal coefficients, not convergence by itself
notes: Everything is assumed finite or locally finite; for Mathieu-type operators the quiver is locally finite, and the perturbed subspace is called analytic.
statement: A locally finite quiver has finitely many paths of any fixed length issuing from a fixed vertex, so the prescribed perturbation coefficient is a finite sum. This is a formal statement. In finite dimensions a spectrally isolated cluster has an analytic spectral projection; for Hill operators bounded polynomial perturbations and the elliptic unperturbed operator give analytic cluster perturbation. Local finiteness alone does not prove convergence for an arbitrary infinite operator.
reconstruction: The analytic claim is confined to a specified operator setting, not inferred from the graph alone.
fate: \citet[section 1, Remark 2]{arnold1983mathieu} explicitly makes this distinction: it treats formal series or finite matrices, and invokes ellipticity for Mathieu convergence.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: The perturbed invariant subspace as a graph
notes: \(V_0(\varepsilon)\) is the graph of \(B(\varepsilon):V_0\to\bigoplus_{i\ne0}V_i\), and equation (7) imposes invariance.
statement: For a finite-dimensional diagonalizable \(\Lambda\) and an isolated eigenvalue \(\lambda_0\), the small perturbed spectral subspace is the graph of an analytic \(B(\varepsilon)\) with \(B(0)=0\), relative to the fixed spectral complement. The invariance equation is \((\Lambda+\varepsilon A)(\iota+B)=(\iota+B)S(\varepsilon)\), where \(\iota:V_0\hookrightarrow V\). This notation avoids treating a projection and an inclusion as the same typed map.
reconstruction: Isolation, fixed complement and the inclusion convention are supplied.
fate: \citet[section 2]{arnold1983mathieu} writes the graph equation. The general perturbation method predates the talk; the Supplement credits \citet{bloch1958perturbations}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: The secular operator preserves the cluster spectrum
notes: The operator \(\lambda_0+\varepsilon\alpha^1+\cdots\) is called secular; restriction to \(V_0(\varepsilon)\) is similar to it.
statement: The effective operator \(S(\varepsilon)=(\iota+B)^{-1}(\Lambda+\varepsilon A)|_{\operatorname{graph}B}(\iota+B)\) acts on the fixed space \(V_0\) and has exactly the perturbed cluster eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity. Analyticity of the matrix S does not by itself imply analyticity of each individual eigenvalue for a general non-self-adjoint family.
reconstruction: The inverse is restricted to the graph and multiplicity is specified; no unsupported eigenvalue-analyticity claim is added.
fate: The similarity and spectrum assertion is explicit in \citet[section 2]{arnold1983mathieu}; the exact notebook formulation matches it.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: Closed paths give universal coefficient formulas
notes: \(\alpha_k=\sum_{|\gamma|=k}\Pi_\gamma(A)Q_\gamma(\Lambda)\), where the loops start and end at zero and Q is rational in eigenvalues.
statement: In the graph-normalized effective operator, the coefficient of \(\varepsilon^k\) is a sum over length-k closed paths at the chosen eigenspace. The factor \(\Pi_\gamma(A)\) is the ordered block product, and \(Q_\gamma\) is a universal rational function of the eigenvalue differences. If several parenthesis fillings yield the same loop, their denominator contributions must be added in \(Q_\gamma\).
reconstruction: Graph normalization and the aggregation of different fillings specify the otherwise ambiguous rational coefficient.
fate: This is \citet[Theorems 1--2 and section 4, Remark 1]{arnold1983mathieu}. His dated Supplement explicitly credits Bloch’s 1958 antecedent for these coefficient results \citep{bloch1958perturbations}; Arnold’s proof was read directly.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: Filled bracket diagrams remember the denominator data
notes: Insert vertices into a bracket symbol; opening parentheses become zeros, closing parentheses are omitted from the solid path, and dashed arrows are then added. Different fillings can have one loop.
statement: Fill each letter slot by a nonzero quiver vertex. Put zero at both ends and at every opening parenthesis to form a solid path; require its arrows to be allowed. Add a dashed arrow from the vertex immediately preceding each closing parenthesis to the zero of its matching opening parenthesis. A symbol of length \(k-1\) yields a loop of k solid arrows. Dashed arrows encode information lost by the solid loop alone.
reconstruction: Admissibility and the exclusion of zero from letter slots are restored from the published definitions.
fate: The definitions and examples are an exact match to \citet[section 4]{arnold1983mathieu}. This is Arnold’s particular diagrammatic construction; the underlying coefficient expansion is older.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: The denominator rule for each filled diagram
notes: Equation (11) sums \(\Pi_{\gamma(I)}(A)/q_I(\Lambda)\); equation (12) multiplies \(\lambda_0-\lambda_i\) for solid arrows into nonzero i and \(\lambda_j-\lambda_0\) for dashed arrows from nonzero j.
statement: For each admissible filling I of length \(k-1\), take exactly the indicated signed product \(q_I\), counting arrows with multiplicity. Its contribution to \(\alpha_k\) is the chronological solid-loop product divided by \(q_I\). Summing over all fillings gives the coefficient. In particular the filling \((i)j\) has denominator \((\lambda_0-\lambda_i)(\lambda_0-\lambda_j)(\lambda_i-\lambda_0)\), agreeing with the notebook example.
reconstruction: The exact sign and multiplicities are retained; no denominator factor is changed.
fate: This is \citet[Theorem 4 and the denominator definition]{arnold1983mathieu}. The Supplement credits the equivalent coefficient theorem to Bloch 1958, while recording Arnold’s distinct parenthesis notation \citep{bloch1958perturbations}.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: Fourier blocks of a trigonometric perturbation
notes: \(V_k=\langle e_k,e_{-k}\rangle\), \(\Lambda=d^2/dt^2\), and equation (16) gives a two by two matrix marked with a question mark.
statement: For \(i,j>0\) and \(A_{ij}:V_i\to V_j\), in the ordered bases \((e_i,e_{-i})\), \((e_j,e_{-j})\), multiplication by \(a(t)=\sum a_se^{ist}\) has block \(\begin{pmatrix}a_{j-i}&a_{i+j}\\a_{-i-j}&a_{i-j}\end{pmatrix}\). The printed signs are correct for that convention. The zero-frequency block has dimension one; odd-numbered tongues instead use the half-integer Fourier lattice.
reconstruction: The zero block and antiperiodic sector are specified; the handwritten question mark does not require a false correction.
fate: \citet[section 3, Lemma 1 and preceding setup]{arnold1983mathieu} gives the same matrix and treats both integer and half-integer frequencies.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: Remote blocks are scalar for an even polynomial
notes: If \(i+j>p\), off-diagonal entries vanish; for \(a_{-s}=a_s\), the block is scalar. Products of scalar blocks remain scalar.
statement: If a has Fourier support \(|s|\le p\) and \(i+j>p\), the off-diagonal block entries vanish. If a is even, the two remaining diagonal entries coincide, so \(A_{ij}=a_{j-i}I\). For a general non-even polynomial the remote block is only diagonal; equality of the summed effective diagonal entries needs the later involution.
reconstruction: The distinction between evenness and reality is explicit: an even polynomial may have complex coefficients.
fate: This is \citet[section 3, Lemma 2 and Remark 2]{arnold1983mathieu}; it is the elementary ingredient of the older even-gap estimate.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: Reflection of a short loop delays splitting
notes: The combinatorial lemma says \(\tau p<2k\) implies \(\alpha_\tau\) is scalar. A loop is reflected across zero at a nonremote arrow.
statement: A loop based at k on the nonnegative frequency lattice, with \(\tau\) arrows each of length at most p, cannot contain an arrow \(i\to j\) with \(i+j\le p\) when \(\tau p<2k\): reflecting the subsequent path would give a path from k to minus k of total length at most \(\tau p\). Hence all factors are remote. For even a, this makes \(\alpha_\tau\) scalar and prevents splitting to that order.
reconstruction: The reflected path is a length argument; the notebook’s parenthetical homotopy language is not needed for a stronger topological theorem.
fate: The proof is exactly \citet[section 3, Lemma 3 and proof of Theorem 3]{arnold1983mathieu}. A labels this short combinatorial proof; the resulting spectral bound itself is E because of Levy--Keller’s 1963 result.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.

title: Dual bracket fillings equalize the diagonal corrections
notes: Opening parentheses split a word into fragments; reverse letters within each fragment with their attached closing parentheses, then restore the opening parentheses. The contributions exchange the diagonal entries.
statement: In the remote-loop regime, this operation is an involution on admissible fillings. Reversed arrows interchange the diagonal entries of the commuting Fourier blocks, while the signed denominator remains unchanged because the letter multiset and its closing-parenthesis multiplicities are preserved. Pairing the contributions therefore makes every effective coefficient below the first allowed splitting order scalar, even for a non-even complex trigonometric polynomial.
reconstruction: The remote-loop restriction and denominator invariance are supplied from the proof. Complex coefficients are allowed, so no Hermitian or positivity assertion is inferred.
fate: \citet[section 5, Lemmas 2--4 and proof of Theorem 7]{arnold1983mathieu} matches the final page. The Supplement attributes the spectral estimate to Hochstadt 1964; A marks the verified involution proof, not a new first proof of the estimate.
present_status: As of November 2026: the stated result is established in the specified setting.
